newsitem.title: USA: US House lawmaker optimistic on moving power bill.
newsitem.headline: US House lawmaker optimistic on moving power bill.

text.p: House energy and power subcommittee chairman Dan Schaefer said Wednesday that efforts to pass a bill to open local power markets to competition were not dead.

The day before a hearing on his bill, which calls for states to break up local utility monopolies by the end of 2000, the Colorado Republican said there had been a resurgence of momentum behind legislation, with the Senate moving faster than expected, and the Clinton administration hoping to have its position ready in July.

"When you have the people on the far right and the far left (supporting it), you know something is going to happen," he said at an energy efficiency conference sponsored by the U.S. Energy Association and Johnson Controls, Inc.

After Thursday's hearing, he said he might hold a "limited numer of subsequent hearings before beginning work on legislation which will become law in the 105th Congress." He has said he wanted his panel to pass a bill in July.
"We'll continue (with hearings) until such time we think we've covered all bases," he said. His panel has held about 14 hearings on electricity restructuring over the last two years.

Schaefer shrugged off comments by key Democrats on the House Commerce Committee, who have said there did not appear to be enough consensus behind power market deregulation to move a bill as early as July.

He told reporters that he was talking to other members of the committee to address their concerns. "We're slowly going through the process, meeting individually with members, seeing what they have as questions," he said.
